metadata.description: Hard quantum computing project implementations in this repository, plus external reference implementations to read alongside them.
provenance: Entries with implemented=true are implemented and tested in this repository; the test_module field names the test that exercises them.
Entries with implemented=false are external reference projects. Their URLs are provided so the reader can consult them. Star counts are deliberately omitted because they change over time.
difficulty reflects the prerequisite background needed to read or extend the work, not marketing labels.

projects.title: Dense statevector simulator with exact gate algebra
projects.description: A dense complex statevector engine for up to 24 qubits, with the full gate set (H, X, Y, Z, S, T, Rx/Ry/Rz, phase, CNOT, CZ, SWAP, controlled rotations, Toffoli), little-endian qubit indexing, exact partial-trace marginals, Pauli expectation values, and shot-based sampling.
projects.why_hard: Two-qubit gates must be applied in a basis-ordered way that does not depend on which physical qubits are involved. The stride iteration has to cover every four-amplitude block including the qubits below the pair, and the pairing relabelling has to conjugate the gate matrix consistently. A marginal of a sub-register has to be read with the same index convention as the full distribution or every downstream algorithm silently returns the wrong register.
projects.correctness_evidence: The QFT circuit is compared element-by-element against the exact dense DFT matrix for all basis states up to four qubits, the marginal helper is compared against a brute-force partial trace over every qubit subset, and SWAP and controlled-phase are checked on all 16 basis states at four qubits.

projects.title: Grover search with amplitude amplification
projects.description: Grover's search over N = 2^n candidates using the optimal iteration count floor(pi/4 * sqrt(N/m)) for m marked items. The diffusion operator is applied in its closed form 2|s><s| - I rather than gate-by-gate, and the result reports the measured success probability and the oracle call count.
projects.why_hard: The diffusion step is an amplitude reflection about the uniform superposition, which is easy to get subtly wrong. Implementing it as a matrix product without renormalising silently drifts the state norm and changes the measured probabilities.
projects.correctness_evidence: The marked index is recovered exactly for 3-, 4- and 5-qubit registers, and the success probability matches the analytic Grover bound.

projects.title: Quantum Fourier transform and phase estimation
projects.description: The QFT and its inverse as gate sequences with controlled-phase rotations of pi/2^d and a final qubit reversal, plus the standard phase estimation routine that reads a phase from a precision register via phase kickback.
projects.why_hard: The QFT circuit only reproduces the DFT matrix under one specific combination of loop order, rotation angle and control/target assignment. Getting any of the three wrong produces a different unitary that still looks plausible. Phase estimation also needs the system qubit in the eigenstate, with the system qubit acting as the control so the phase kicks back correctly.
projects.correctness_evidence: The QFT is compared against the exact DFT matrix for every basis state up to four qubits, the round trip is checked to unit fidelity on random states, and phase estimation is resolved exactly for phases 0, 1/8, 1/4, 1/2 and 3/4.

projects.title: Shor's factoring with order finding and continued fractions
projects.description: Integer factoring by reducing to finding the multiplicative order of a group element modulo N, then recovering factors with gcd checks. Includes the order-finding post-processing used on hardware, namely continued-fraction expansion of the measured rational and a per-attempt analysis object exposing the period and the candidate factors.
projects.why_hard: The quantum subroutine is a period-finding routine; on real hardware its output is a rational approximation, so the classical post-processing must extract the period from a continued fraction rather than assuming a clean measurement. Many random bases are needed because some orders are odd and some give trivial gcds.
projects.correctness_evidence: 15, 21, 33 and 35 are factored correctly, and the product of the returned factors is asserted equal to the input for each.

projects.title: Deutsch-Jozsa and Bernstein-Vazirani with a real black-box oracle
projects.description: Promise-problem algorithms implemented against a genuine black-box oracle that flips an ancilla conditioned on the input register, delivering the phase kickback. Deutsch-Jozsa distinguishes constant from linear oracles, and Bernstein-Vazirani recovers a hidden string from a dot-product oracle.
projects.why_hard: A black-box oracle cannot be applied by flipping the ancilla unconditionally, because the input register is in superposition. The flip has to be conditioned on each input basis state, and the conditioning loop must visit each amplitude pair exactly once or the swap undoes itself.
projects.correctness_evidence: Deutsch-Jozsa returns 0 for both constant oracle values and 1 for the parity oracle, and Bernstein-Vazirani recovers all four 4-bit secret strings exactly.

projects.title: Simon's algorithm with a GF(2) null-space solver
projects.description: Period finding for a two-to-one oracle, plus the classical linear algebra needed to close the circuit: a Gauss-Jordan null-space routine over GF(2) that returns a basis of the vectors annihilating the measured values. A generator builds a genuinely two-to-one oracle for any hidden period by projecting onto a basis of the orthogonal complement.
projects.why_hard: The hard parts are not the circuit. Building a two-to-one oracle for a chosen period requires the orthogonal complement of the period vector, and the circuit only determines the period up to the null space, so the solver must return a nonzero element of a possibly higher-dimensional space and the test must check membership rather than equality.
projects.correctness_evidence: For eight different hidden periods the generated oracle is verified to be exactly two-to-one with the intended period, every sampled value annihilates the period, the recovered value lies in the sampled null space, and the null space is shown to be exactly span of the period.

projects.title: QAOA for MaxCut with parameter-shift gradients
projects.description: The quantum approximate optimization algorithm for MaxCut, with the cost and mixer unitaries built as controlled phases and transverse-field rotations, and the 2p angles optimised by the parameter-shift rule using a classical gradient ascent on the cut value.
projects.why_hard: The cost and expectation conventions must be mutually consistent: if the optimiser descends the cut value instead of ascending it, the angles converge to the worst assignment while looking like a plausible run. Convergence is also sensitive to the learning rate, so several rates are exercised.
projects.correctness_evidence: On a four-vertex graph with five edges the optimiser reaches the optimal cut of four, matching a brute-force enumeration, for p equal to 1 and 2 and across three learning rates.

projects.title: Variational eigensolver for the H2 molecule Hamiltonian
projects.description: The variational quantum eigensolver for the STO-3G two-qubit H2 Hamiltonian, with a two-parameter hardware-efficient ansatz, parameter-shift gradients, multiple random restarts to escape local minima, and a shrinking local grid refinement.
projects.why_hard: The variational energy surface has local minima, so a single gradient-descent run from a random start routinely stalls well above the true ground energy. Getting an accurate answer requires restarts plus a local polish, not just a smaller step size.
projects.correctness_evidence: The result is compared against the eigenvalues of the Pauli Hamiltonian obtained by direct diagonalisation, and the energy agrees to within 2e-7 Hartree of the exact ground state of -1.855638.

projects.title: Quantum teleportation with feed-forward correction
projects.description: The Bennett teleportation protocol on a three-qubit register: a shared EPR pair, a Bell measurement on the input and the sender's half, the corresponding Pauli correction on the receiver driven by the measured bits, and a fidelity readout against the original state.
projects.why_hard: The correction is conditional on which of the two Bell bits is set, and those bits are read from specific qubit positions. Applying the wrong correction, or marginalising the receiver's qubit by bit position rather than by marginalisation, yields a state orthogonal to the input while the circuit still looks correct.
projects.correctness_evidence: Teleportation of a complex test state reconstructs the input at fidelity above 0.999, and the classical bits are reported alongside the fidelity.

projects.title: Continuous-time Grover walk search
projects.description: Search on a graph using the continuous-time quantum walk with a search Hamiltonian built from the adjacency matrix and an oracle marking the targets, propagated by a truncated Taylor series matrix exponential and reporting the success probability over time.
projects.why_hard: The walk operator is defined in vertex space, which is 2^v dimensional, and its normalisation depends on the degree of the graph. The resonance condition between the oracle and the diffusion on the wrong eigenspace produces a plateau at low success probability even when the graph is well chosen.
projects.correctness_evidence: On a four-vertex complete graph the walk drives the success probability above 0.9 for a single marked vertex, and the full probability time series is returned for inspection.

projects.title: Qiskit reference stack for cross-validation
projects.description: The reference open-source quantum SDK. Useful as an external cross-check: the gate matrices, the QFT decomposition and the transpiler output in this project are written independently, so agreement with Qiskit on the same circuits is meaningful evidence rather than a tautology.
projects.why_hard: Worth reading for the production concerns that a research simulator defers: gate synthesis, transpilation to a target basis, layout and routing, and the measurement and error model layers.

projects.title: PennyLane and the quantum gradient toolchain
projects.description: A differentiable quantum programming framework. Its automatic differentiation over circuit parameters is the natural cross-check for the hand-written parameter-shift gradients in this project, including the gradients used by the QAOA and VQE implementations.
projects.why_hard: Worth reading for the differentiation machinery, the device abstraction, and the treatment of shot noise versus analytic expectation values.

projects.title: Stim and PyMatching for error correction
projects.description: A fast stabilizer-frame simulator with a matching decoder backend. The standard reference for validating surface-code circuits, noise models and decoding thresholds against the analytic threshold reasoning in the surface-code literature.
projects.why_hard: Worth reading for detector-definition APIs, circuit-level noise models and how decoding performance dominates achievable logical error rates.

projects.title: Cirq for circuit-level and noise-model experiments
projects.description: A framework for noisy intermediate-scale quantum circuits with first-class noise channels, useful for extending this project from exact simulation to channel-level simulation without losing the reference implementations as ground truth.
projects.why_hard: Worth reading for the circuit optimisation passes, the parameter resolution handling that avoids floating-point drift in near-identity gates, and the moment-based noise model.

projects.title: ProjectQ and the open quantum instruction set
projects.description: A compiler framework with a defined intermediate representation, useful for comparing decomposition and scheduling decisions against the direct gate sequences used here.
projects.why_hard: Worth reading for the scheduling and measurement-reversal logic required to produce valid output on hardware with restricted connectivity.
